An accident occurred on 21.10.2015 between two motorcycles.
The claimant was the rider of one motorcycle who suffered injuries and, as a result, he initiated proceedings seeking compensation.

sentences.text:
The Tribunal on assessment of the evidence has recorded a finding that the accident did take place and for the occurrence of the accident, the claimant was responsible to the extent of 30%,
while the rider of the other motorcycle was responsible to the extent of 70%.
3. The Tribunal has thereafter proceeded to award a sum of Rs.2,93,067/- as compensation.
Being aggrieved by this award, both the claimant as well as the insurer are in appeal.

4. The insurer contends that since the complaint was lodged by the rider of the other motorcycle and a charge sheet was also laid against the claimant as NC: 2024:KHC:51364 well as the rider of the other motorcycle, attribution of negligence to the extent of 30:70 was incorrect.

5. It is also sought to be contended that the compensation awarded was excessive and that the accident occurred at the edge of the road, which indicated that the claimant had come over to the wrong side of the road and had caused the accident and, therefore, the entire negligence ought to have been attributed only on the claimant.

6. The claimant on the other hand contends that the rider of the other motorcycle who was examined as RW.1 has categorically admitted that the charge sheet had been laid against the rider of the other motorcycle as well as the claimant and the other motorcycle rider had pleaded guilty before the Criminal Court and, therefore, attribution of negligence to the extent of just 70% on the rider of the other motorcycle was incorrect.
It is also NC: 2024:KHC:51364 contended that the compensation awarded was inadequate.

7. As far as the question of negligence is concerned, it is no doubt true that the complaint was lodged by the rider of the other motorcycle, but ultimately the Police have laid the charge sheet against both the riders of the motorcycle.

The evidence on record also clearly establishes that both the claimant as well as the rider of the other motorcycle had admitted guilt before the Criminal Court and had paid the respective fines imposed against them.
It is therefore clear that both of them had admitted that they were the cause of the accident.
8. In that view of the matter, the attribution of negligence to the extent of 30:70 on the claimant and on the insurer of the other motorcycle cannot be found fault with.

As far as composition is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the whole body disability at 12%
even though the doctor had stated that the whole body disability was 24.5%.
10.
The claimant had admittedly suffered a fracture of the femur which is a major bone.

In my view,
therefore, it would be appropriate to treat the whole body disability at 15% as against 12%
determined by the Tribunal.
11. As there was no proof of actual income, the Tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.8,000/-.

In such cases, as the accident was of the year 2015, the notional income of Rs.9,000/- as Sri Dinesh vs Sri Rakshith Nayak on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104019873/
4 determined by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority will have to be adopted.

sentences.text:
Consequently,
the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,75,400/- (Rs.9,000/- X 12 X 17 X 15%) towards 'loss of future earnings'.

The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/-
towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.20,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.

In my view, having regard to the fact that the claimant had suffered a major fracture, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.75,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.75,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.
13. The Tribunal has taken the laid-up period as 3 months.
In my view, it would be appropriate to treat the laid-up period as 4 months and award a sum of Rs.36,000/- (Rs.9,000/- X 4 months).

14. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.48,979/-
towards medical expenses and Rs.18,000/- towards future medical expenses.
These sums are just and proper and are affirmed.

15. As the claimant was hospitalized for 8 days, it would be appropriate to award a sum of Rs.15,000/-
NC: 2024:KHC:51364 towards conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges as against a sum of Rs.5,000/-.
16.

Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the following sums are awarded as compensation:

17. Accordingly, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.5,43,379/- as against Rs.2,93,067/-.

Since the claimant had contributed to the extent of 50% to the accident, he would be entitled to only half of the said compensation i.e., Rs.2,71,690/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation.
18. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
19. These appeals are accordingly disposed of.
